newsitem.title: USA: PIA sees weak Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: PIA sees weak Q2 results.

text.p: PIA Merchandising Services Inc warned Thursday that its second quarter results would be substantially below analysts' estimates.

Analysts had expected the company would post a loss of $0.05 a share for the second quarter, ending June 30, according to First Call. In the comparable year-ago period the company had profits of $206,000, or $0.03 a share, on revenues of $26.8 million.
The company reiterated that operating results for the remainder of the year will be substantially below last year's results despite increasing revenues.

As a result of the weaker results PIA said it will institute cost cutting measures to streamline the company and bring expenses more in line with revenues. PIA said that as a result it expects to take restructuring charges in either its second or third quarter.

The company also said it has appointed Terry Peets as president and chief executive. Chairman Clinton Owens has relinquished the chief executive post to concentrate on the strategic direction of the company. The position of president has been vacant for a number of months since Tom Goff resigned to pursue other interests.
The company also said its Chief Financial Officer Roy Olofson has resigned and a replacement is being sought.
Peets joins PIA from grocery retailer The Vons Cos Inc where he was executive vice president.
